answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The sparrow multiplier is published, charged in cedar, and shale lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 885 identities would post 1625 proofs and burn roughly 4 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
